**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Delete hot vectors for non-indexable replacements**

When an ordinary event with indexed text is replayed under the same ID with empty text, or changes to `graph.node`/`graph.edge`, this predicate becomes false and no replacement or deletion is issued for its existing hot-vector rows. Vector search can therefore continue returning the removed text and old metadata; if the previous vector carried a retention-exempt label, it can remain indefinitely. Reconcile the parent’s hot vectors even when the replacement produces no new vector entries.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Version detached vector replacements**

When two ingests replace the same event ID before the first embedding finishes, both detached tasks eventually call `replaceMongoVectorEntries`, and the older task can finish last and overwrite the newer text’s vectors. Fresh evidence beyond the resolved timeout thread is that `backgroundIndexing` is still explicitly detached here while replacement writes have no authoritative text hash or generation predicate. Serialize writes per parent or condition them on the current event version.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Key hydration cache entries by the computed text hash**

When a filesystem-backed item omits an explicit `content_hash`, reindexing changed content at the same source path leaves the hydration cache keyed only by that path. This lookup then returns the old full text for up to the cache TTL; the new row’s chunk hash rejects the stale slice and search returns an empty document instead of rereading the file. Pass `doc.text_hash_sha256` as the fallback content hash so each indexed revision receives a distinct hydration cache key.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Deduplicate identical event IDs before processing**

When a batch contains the same event payload twice, this preflight accepts both entries because only conflicting payloads are rejected. The main loop then appends the ID and accepted event twice, repeats projection work, reports `count: 2` for one stored event, and exposes two entries for downstream fan-out such as Kafka. Collapse identical IDs after validation or reject every duplicate ID.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve labels in native vector-search results**

When a partition’s Atlas search index is ready, this `$project` omits `labels`, even though `toMetadata` later reads `doc.labels`; the native path therefore returns `labels: []` for every hit while the cosine fallback preserves them. Consumers using labels for retention or categorization consequently observe different metadata depending only on index readiness. Include `labels: 1` in the native projection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Strip Mongo storage IDs from policy updates**

When a caller reads a policy with `getPolicy`, edits it, and passes that returned object to `setPolicy`, the payload includes MongoDB’s `_id`; spreading it into `doc` causes the subsequent `$set` to attempt to update the immutable `_id` field and the otherwise valid policy update fails. Remove `_id` alongside `created_at` before issuing the update.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate unavailable historical embedding models**

When a persisted partition references a model that the current provider no longer serves, this unguarded `generate` call rejects the entire vector search, including results already obtained from healthy current-model partitions. Partition metadata is retained after model configuration changes and even after its rows are deleted, so one obsolete model can keep all vector retrieval unavailable until manual cleanup. Catch failures per partition and skip or mark the unavailable partition while continuing with the others.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve reference-first storage after text normalization**

For filesystem-backed text whose indexing normalization changes coordinates—such as CRLF files, tab-indented content, or HTML converted to Markdown—this exact raw-slice check disables source redaction and stores the full normalized chunk inline. The hydration path already knows how to validate normalized-coordinate chunks, so these common inputs unexpectedly bypass the reference-first representation and duplicate source content in vector collections. Record normalized coordinates explicitly or map the normalized chunks back to raw offsets instead of silently abandoning redaction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cap visibility-mode session reads**

When a caller supplies a very large positive `limit` in visibility mode, this branch forwards it directly to MongoDB without the 1,000-row cap used by resume mode or any other upper bound. A single request can therefore scan and serialize an arbitrarily large session history’s `extra` fields, causing excessive database and response memory use. Clamp this limit to a bounded maximum before calling `getSessionEvents`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
